The review step is not reliable. It says to 'navigate to' /?category=Wrok from /?category=Home and expect Go back to land on Home. The app has no link to a broken URL, so the only way to get there is by typing it, and a typed navigation has an empty document.referrer. The script (src/index.js brokenLinkPage) then falls through to href="/", so the step would land on `/`, not Home. The script also adds a `history.length > 1` condition that the spec does not mention, though it is harmless. No automated test covers the behaviour, and I cannot run a browser here.

findings.what: The AC-10 'verified by review' step cannot produce its stated result. Typing /?category=Wrok in the same tab gives an empty document.referrer, so the script does not call history.back() and Go back lands on `/`, not /?category=Home. The step does not say how to reach the broken URL with a same-origin referrer, and the app has no link to one. No review record of the step being run was provided.
findings.fix: Rewrite the review step so it produces a same-origin referrer. For example, from /?category=Home run `location.href='/?category=Wrok'` in the console, or follow a link from a page of the app, and then click Go back. Run it and record the result. Or add an automated browser test.

findings.what: The Go back script also requires `history.length > 1`. The spec's decision describes only a same-origin referrer and rejects `history.length > 1` as the criterion. This is an undocumented extra condition.
findings.fix: Remove the condition, or record it in the spec's 'Go back' decision.

findings.what: The Go back script is only checked by a regex on its text (document.referrer, location.origin, history.back()). A broken condition in the script would still pass, so the test does not exercise its behaviour.
findings.fix: Accept this because the spec marks the behaviour as verified by review, or run the script in a small DOM stub.
